rationale:
The requirement applies. `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with `name:` front matter, so it is a site.

The obligation is that each link to a file holding specialized material must say when to read it. The file has no Markdown links. It points to two other files in inline code:
- **`references/review-prompt.md`:** Step 3 of the Workflow names the file in "Tell it to read this skill's `references/review-prompt.md` ...". That is the trigger: when starting a review subagent for a requirement group in step 3. If this counts as a link, it says when to read the file.
- **`references/fixme.md`:** The text in "Choosing references" reads "To defer a gap the user agrees to, use `{fixme}` as the habeas-evidence skill's `references/fixme.md` describes." That ties it to the situation of deferring an agreed gap. This file belongs to another skill. If it counts as a link, it also says when to read the file.

Other mentions, such as the habeas-evidence skill's "Rules" and "Uncovered Rust items" sections and "Disagreeing assessments", are references to sections of other skills. They are not file links. Each also states its trigger, for example "For an item still uncovered after that, see ...".

So the file has no link that lacks a stated reading condition, and there are no violation matches to judge.

text: A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
